results.summary_before: This design blinks the eight output LEDs in various patterns, with a function switch selecting between a simple blinky mode and a double 14-bit counter mode. In counter mode, two output control switches select which bits of the counters are shown, and a pause switch halts counting. The design is intended to work with the mcpi module, likely as an external display or counter. The documentation is minimal, with no explanation of the internal implementation.

results.summary_before: This project implements a small microcontroller with a subset of the PIC mid-range instruction set, including six general-purpose registers and 16 program words, but no special function registers, carry, or call/stack support. Programs are shifted in serially through prog_data with prog_strobe, using a 28-bit word per instruction, after which the device runs standalone. Four general-purpose inputs and eight general-purpose outputs are provided, with GPR 6 and GPR 7 mapped to GPI and GPO. External hardware is needed only at startup to shift in the program, such as another microcontroller or USB GPIO interface.

results.summary_before: This chip is a scalable synchronous 4-bit tri-directional loadable counter that can count up, down, or pause, and supports loading a new count value. It is intended to be usable as a program counter, for example to set the next address for a jump instruction. The design is implemented using mixed radix circuit synthesis (MRCS) and Wokwi, and it can be tested by resetting the state, setting the direction and count enable, and clocking the circuit. No external hardware is needed.

results.summary_before: This design implements a finite state machine that counts from 0 to 3, with the count advanced by a button press when the first input is enabled. The count is displayed on a seven-segment display, and other inputs provide additional logic for experimentation. It is a copy of the author's earlier Tiny Tapeout submission and is intended for use on a Steam Deck. Testing requires enabling the first input, turning off all others, and pressing the button to progress the FSM.

results.summary_before: This design implements a small R-2R digital-to-analog converter by adding a resistor ladder to the outputs of D flip-flops. It is tested by attaching an external R-2R ladder and a non-inverting op-amp to the output to observe the analog voltage. The design requires external resistors and an op-amp, and the documentation notes that an AND gate was removed and a pin is used as a passthrough. The project is a simple mixed-signal experiment.
